name: Spaghetti Bolognese
description: A rich beef Bolognese with onion, carrot and celery, tossed with spaghetti and finished with Parmesan.
instructions: Finely dice the onion, carrot and celery. Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat and cook the vegetables for 8–10 minutes until soft and lightly golden.
Add the crushed garlic and 1 tsp dried oregano and cook for 30 seconds. Stir in the tomato purée and cook for 2 minutes until it darkens slightly.
Increase the heat to medium-high, add the beef mince and season with salt and black pepper. Cook for 6–8 minutes, breaking it up thoroughly, until well browned with no pink remaining.

Add the canned tomatoes, 200 ml prepared beef stock and 2 tsp Worcestershire sauce. Bring to a simmer, then cook uncovered over low heat for 30–40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until rich and thick.
Boil the spaghetti in well-salted water until al dente. Reserve a mugful of pasta water, then drain.
Taste and season the Bolognese. Toss the spaghetti through the sauce, adding a splash of pasta water if needed so the sauce coats it evenly.
Serve immediately with the grated Parmesan and plenty of black pepper.
Cook the onion, carrot and celery in olive oil until soft, then add the garlic, dried oregano and tomato purée.
Brown the beef mince thoroughly, breaking it up well, until no pink remains.
Add the canned tomatoes, prepared beef stock and Worcestershire sauce. Simmer uncovered for 30–40 minutes until rich and thick, then season to taste.
make_ahead.storage: Cool promptly in a shallow container, cover and refrigerate within two hours for up to 48 hours.
day_of: Reheat the Bolognese sauce until steaming throughout, stirring frequently and adding a splash of water if it has thickened.
Boil the spaghetti fresh, toss it through the reheated sauce and finish with Parmesan and black pepper.
